label: The Paleolithic Era ends as the retreat of the last glaciers drives the global transition toward farming and permanent human settlements.
The Han Dynasty establishes formal trade routes to the West, opening the Silk Road and initiating centuries of Eurasian cultural exchange.
Norse mariners establish a settlement in modern-day Canada, representing the earliest known European transatlantic voyage.
The Mexica people found the city of Tenochtitlan, establishing the geopolitical foundation for the expansion of the Aztec Empire.
Maritime trade routes bring the second plague pandemic to Europe, permanently altering the demographic and economic structure of the continent.
Johannes Gutenberg develops the movable-type printing press in Germany, introducing a systemic system of mass communication to Europe.
A maritime expedition arrives in the Caribbean, initiating sustained interaction and globalization between Europe and the Americas.
The Industrial Revolution begins in Great Britain, marking the historic transition from agrarian economies to machine-driven manufacturing.
The first wave of the Industrial Revolution draws to a close as steam power, mass metallurgy, and railway networks become mature global realities.
The British Parliament enacts the Slave Trade Act, marking a significant legal step toward the eventual global prohibition of the transatlantic slave trade.
Harriet Tubman escapes bondage and begins a decade-long series of rescue missions to guide enslaved people along the Underground Railroad.
The Space Age begins as the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, successfully reaches orbit and transmits radio signals back to Earth.
The opening of the Berlin Wall begins, initiating the collapse of Eastern Bloc regimes and symbolising the approaching conclusion of the Cold War.
The Information Age takes root globally as digital computing and commercial internet infrastructure transition society into a networked economy.
A global shift toward green energy accelerates, marking the period where solar and wind power begin scaling to rival fossil fuel grids worldwide.

title: Completion of the Great Pyramid
context_description: The Great Pyramid of Giza is completed for Pharaoh Khufu, remaining the world's tallest man-made structure for over 3,800 years and showcasing advanced engineering.

title: Appointment of Enheduanna
context_description: Enheduanna is appointed High Priestess of the moon god Nanna, writing religious hymns that make her the earliest individual author recorded by name in human history.

title: Enactment of Hammurabi's Code
context_description: King Hammurabi enacts a public stone stela of laws, establishing one of the earliest and most complete surviving written legal codes governing civil and criminal justice.

title: Ascension of Pharaoh Hatshepsut
context_description: Hatshepsut ascends the throne as a female Pharaoh, initiating a prosperous period marked by internal stability, architectural innovation, and extensive regional trade.

title: Uprising of the Trưng Sisters
context_description: The Trưng Sisters lead a popular military uprising against Han Dynasty governors, briefly establishing an autonomous state and becoming symbols of Vietnamese resistance.

title: Standardisation of Paper Production
context_description: Han official Cai Lun standardises papermaking using plant fibres, mulberry bark, and rags, fundamentally transforming global communication and record-keeping.

title: The Death of Hypatia
context_description: Mathematician and philosopher Hypatia is killed during intense religious and socio-political conflict, marking a symbolic end to classical Alexandria's intellectual era.

title: Proclamation of the Wu Zhou Dynasty
context_description: Empress Wu Zetian officially proclaims her independent dynasty, seizing absolute power to become the only female monarch to rule China in her own right.

title: Foundation of Baghdad
context_description: The Abbasid Caliphate founds Baghdad as its capital, rapidly expanding it into a prominent global intellectual hub that will host the famous House of Wisdom.

title: Institutionalisation of the House of Wisdom
context_description: Baghdad's Grand Library transitions into a formal intellectual academy, translating Greek, Persian, and Indian mathematical and scientific texts for global dissemination.

title: Earliest Teaching at Oxford
context_description: Historical records document formal scholastic lectures by visiting scholars, laying early groundwork for structured scientific and mathematical education in Europe.

title: Chartering of the University of Bologna
context_description: Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa grants the Authentica Habita charter, formally establishing Bologna as a center of independent study and pioneering the modern degree.

title: Recognition of the University of Paris
context_description: Masters and students receive official charter recognition, transforming Paris into a premier destination for studying the mathematical sciences and theology.

title: Sealing of the Magna Carta
context_description: King John seals the Magna Carta under pressure from rebel barons, establishing the constitutional precedent that even the sovereign is subject to the rule of law.

title: Relief of the Siege of Orléans
context_description: Joan of Arc successfully rallies French forces to break the English siege, entirely reversing the strategic momentum of the Hundred Years' War.

title: Return of the Victoria
context_description: The Victoria returns under Juan Sebastián Elcano, completing the first documented human circumnavigation of the Earth after an arduous three-year global voyage.

title: Ascension of Queen Nzinga
context_description: Queen Nzinga assumes the throne of Ndongo, launching decades of military campaigns and strategic diplomacy to resist Portuguese expansion into Central Africa.

title: Chartering of the Royal Society
context_description: King Charles II seals the official charter for the Royal Society, formalising an elite academy of natural philosophers and standardising scientific peer-review.

title: Foundation of the Académie des Sciences
context_description: King Louis XIV establishes the Académie des Sciences, providing heavily funded institutional structure that formalised mathematical physics and celestial mechanics.

title: Introduction of the Watt Steam Engine
context_description: James Watt deploys his commercial condenser steam engine at industrial factories, offering a vastly more efficient method of generating mechanical work.

title: The Storming of the Bastille
context_description: Revolutionary citizens assault and capture the Bastille fortress, sparking social restructuring and accelerating the global decline of absolute feudal monarchies.

title: Lovelace's Analytical Engine Notes
context_description: Ada Lovelace completes elaborate annotations on Babbage's mechanical computer, engineering the world's first complex algorithm designed for machine computation.

title: First International Congress of Mathematicians
context_description: The premier global convention of research mathematicians convenes, establishing a permanent international community to standardise and coordinate mathematical research.

title: Presentation of the Hilbert Problems
context_description: David Hilbert challenges mathematics at the Sorbonne Congress, presenting 23 foundational unsolved problems that guided research throughout the twentieth century.

title: First Female Nobel Prize Laureate
context_description: Marie Curie is co-awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for her rigorous research into radioactive isolation methods, breaking institutional barriers for women scientists.

title: The Suffragist March on Parliament
context_description: Political suffragists march on Parliament to protest stalled voting rights legislation, facing heavy resistance and escalating the global women's suffrage movement.

title: Outbreak of World War I
context_description: Austria-Hungary fires opening artillery across the Danube against Serbian forces, initiating a major global industrial conflict that fundamentally redrew political maps.

title: Outbreak of World War II
context_description: Germany invades Poland, triggering declarations of war from Britain and France. This marks the outbreak of World War II, a global conflict that fundamentally reshaped international relations, technology, and geography.

title: Rosa Parks Bus Action
context_description: Rosa Parks refuses to move in a segregated bus section, sparking the Montgomery Bus Boycott that catalysed the modern Civil Rights Movement in the United States.

title: Launch of Vostok 6
context_description: Cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launches into multi-day Earth orbit, successfully completing a mission that makes her the first woman in space.

title: Discovery of Artemisinin
context_description: Medical researcher Tu Youyou extracts artemisinin from sweet wormwood plants, developing a potent antimalarial drug that saved millions of lives globally.

title: Establishment of the United Nations
context_description: The UN charter takes effect, creating an international organization designed to enforce collective security and prevent future global conflicts.

title: First Demonstration of the Transistor
context_description: Bell Labs successfully tests the first working point-contact transistor, providing the fundamental semiconductor building block for all modern electronics.

title: Launch of the World Wide Web
context_description: Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first public description of the World Wide Web project, making the internet accessible via browser software to the public.
